_about: What's new in each release, for players: Settings > Ship software (the update notice) and Version history (web/ota.js). 1 to 3 short lines each, plain words, second person, no story spoilers, no technical terms. Checked by game/tools/ota/whatsnew.py; tools/build_release.py puts a release's lines in its version.json (signed with the release) and its index.json entry; whatsnew.py --index fills older entries.
0.3.0-ota-phone: Hail a crewmate: send a short hail, and your ship passes it to theirs when the two are in range.
Your ship's light flickers when a hail lands. Turn that off in Settings with Flicker for hails.
Test light now runs for 10 seconds, Settings shows what's new in each version, and updates install more reliably.
0.2.7-ota-phone: If something goes wrong, your ship starts in a simple safe mode, so it can still take an update.
Turning the Ship light on or off is now safe even if the power cuts out at that moment.
0.2.6-ota-phone: New in Settings: Test light. Tap it to watch your ship's light blink, even with the Ship light off.
0.2.5-ota-phone: Change your code: pick a new 4-digit sign-in code in Settings.
The charging bolt now shows within seconds of plugging your ship in.
0.2.4-ota-phone: A step-by-step guide to putting the game on your phone's home screen.
0.2.3-ota-phone: Settings, behind the gear: your ship's software, the Ship light and signing out, all in one place.
Reset this ship lets you start it over from the beginning.
Opening the game from your home screen looks cleaner, with a proper launch screen.
0.2.2-ota-phone: Updates now reach your ship through your phone: no cables, no opening the case.
0.2.0-lv-test: The game now runs from your ship's built-in software, so more of the crew can play at the same time.
0.1.0-lv-test: The Long Voyage on your ship: sign in on your phone with your code and play.
Your phone speaks to you as you, and your first day starts with a briefing.
The ship's light breathes softly when something is waiting for you.
